subject: simulating biogeography under a DEC model

messages.author: d3c9ac62d374695a
messages.subject: simulating biogeography under a DEC model
parts:
Dear Nick,

I am hoping to simulate biogeographies onto a tree given a particular model (e.g. DEC). I have been looking at BioGeoBEARS_simulate_v1.R, and I think that I have it somewhat figured out, but I have a few questions:

1) The output of this script is a vector of biogeography states that equals length(phylo$tip.label)+phylo$Nnode, but I'm unsure how to assign the states to the appropriate node/tip. How should I go about doing this?

2) Ultimately, I would like to build stochastic maps for these simulated biogeographies. Presumably, I would need to fit the DEC model to the simulated dataset while fixing states at the nodes (as per http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#feb2014_fixnodes), or somehow create a results_object that fixes the parameter values in addition to the node values before passing it to the stochastic mapping script. Does this sound reasonable, or do you think there would be a better way to proceed?

3) I'd like to simulate biogeographies under a few different scenarios (e.g., reducing the rate of sympatric speciation relative to allopatric speciation). I think that the way to do this is to tinker with the COO_probs_columnar input. I am probably missing some documentation somewhere, but is there someplace that describes how to construct this object (e.g., how to properly construct/interpret Rcpp_leftprobs and Rcpp_rightprobs)?

Thanks in advance!

Jonathan

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] simulating biogeography under a DEC model
parts: Hi -- I'm giving a talk today and then returning to Australia so I will be out of commission for awhile.The simulation code is not fully documented. Your best bet in the short term is to get the zipfile of the scripts for the Matzke 2014 paper, which I think is on PhyloWiki, and try to get that to run...

On Fri, Jan 15, 2016 at 4:20 AM, Jonathan Drury <jonathan...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Nick,

I am hoping to simulate biogeographies onto a tree given a particular model (e.g. DEC). I have been looking at BioGeoBEARS_simulate_v1.R, and I think that I have it somewhat figured out, but I have a few questions:

1) The output of this script is a vector of biogeography states that equals length(phylo$tip.label)+phylo$Nnode, but I'm unsure how to assign the states to the appropriate node/tip. How should I go about doing this?
My memory is hazy, if I was making life easy, these are just in the same order as the tips, then nodes, of the phylo object.

2) Ultimately, I would like to build stochastic maps for these simulated biogeographies. Presumably, I would need to fit the DEC model to the simulated dataset while fixing states at the nodes (as per http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#feb2014_fixnodes), or somehow create a results_object that fixes the parameter values in addition to the node values before passing it to the stochastic mapping script. Does this sound reasonable, or do you think there would be a better way to proceed?

Fixnodes has nothing to do with it, so ignore that. The simulation code, at least the macroevolutionary version of it (which includes speciation/extinction), had plotting code that produced the simulation animations on PhyloWiki.

3) I'd like to simulate biogeographies under a few different scenarios (e.g., reducing the rate of sympatric speciation relative to allopatric speciation). I think that the way to do this is to tinker with the COO_probs_columnar input. I am probably missing some documentation somewhere, but is there someplace that describes how to construct this object (e.g., how to properly construct/interpret Rcpp_leftprobs and Rcpp_rightprobs)?

Rcpp_leftprobs etc. can just be a vector of 1s, the length of the states list. COO_probs_columnar is generated in cladoRcpp.

Good luck, this part of the code is not for the faint of heart...

Cheers, Nick

 

Thanks in advance!

Jonathan

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] simulating biogeography under a DEC model
parts:
Dear Nick,

Thanks very much for your response!

It looks like the macroevolutionary version of the simulation code (BioGeoBEARS_SSEsim_v1.R) does exactly what I’m looking for, since it returns tables that are formatted like the RES_clado_events_tables and RES_ana_events_tables that are produced with the stochastic mapping scripts. 

However, I haven’t been able to figure out how to plot one of the realizations of the SSE simulation. It looks like plot_simDEC_DECJ_inferences plots models that are fit to the simulated datasets (or at least, this function requires a file dej_params.Rdata, which I can’t find and I’m not sure how to generate), and I think the other plotting functions produce barplots like those in the supplementary material for your 2014 Sys Bio paper. I am probably missing something or misinterpreting the code, but when you have a moment, could you steer me in the right direction?

Thanks again for your help—safe travels and good luck clock shifting,

Jonathan

parts:
Hi Jonathan -- I'm digging out and way behind on several deadlines so I won't have time to dig on this for quite awhile. Briefly, the key thing you need to do is find the script that ran the other functions, I don't remember what it is called though. Working through that will show what all the inputs/outputs are, with minimal work. dej_params.Rdata must be something like the result of save() on a data.frame containing inferred or user-decided d, e, and j, but I don't remember specifically. 

If, after finding the run script and making a serious effort with it, it's all still not working for you, I can dig on it, but it may be weeks from now.  Apologies for being brief, I would like to provide full tutorials on these things but the simulation code was a supplemental data archive for a publication; it is vaguely in my plans to officially include this in the package, but it is way down below other much more basic updates that are needed (and also not done yet!).

Cheers, Nick
